body:
> broken in 4.7 master

Extracting the commit from the screenshot for clarity: 7dac0bc3b.

Reproducible with current master on macOS 26.2 in M4 Pro. Only reproducible with clean project, and not always, it seems to be import issue (bunch of threads stuck in `cvtt::Internal::BC7Computer`). I'll bisect it.

> I'll bisect it.

It is reproducible with 4.6-stable custom build as well, so it's either a pre-existing timing issue only reproducible with debug builds, or it's BC7 compressor is just extremely slow with debug build.

Optimized build of current master loads project in the same time as 4.6 and works fine (no errors).
Debug build also works but takes about 3-4 minutes to load, so it's just debug build performance issue.

*Edit:*
> *no errors*

*There's single `ERROR: Bug: Dictionary::operator[] used when there was no value for the given key "colormap". Please report.` in the log, but it's the same in 4.6.*

> There's single `ERROR: Bug: Dictionary::operator[] used when there was no value for the given key "colormap". Please report.` in the log, but it's the same in 4.6.

Yeah I reported this in #115899.

---

I'm mostly wondering about the "timeout waiting for fence" Metal error which seems like a bug, even if the root of the problem is just a slow import due to lacking optimization.

As for the slow import without optimization, it's worth looking into to see if there are some low hanging fruits to restore some usability also for engine contributors. I had a similar issue during the 4.6 cycle which turned out to be a regression (#113172). Some options:
- Profile what's so slow and try to do some manual optimizations to avoid the most pathological cases.
- Force a minimal optimization level for the relevant code (e.g `-Og` or `-O1` if it's enough to resolve most of the performance issue).
- Default `dev_build=yes` to `optimize=debug` (`-Og`) instead of `optimize=none` (`-O0`). The main reason to use `none` is for compilation speed, so this should be benchmarked to see what's the tradeoff between compilation speed, debug information available for debuggers, and performance.
- If the issue is in thirdparty code, we could also consider forcing a minimal optimization level on all thirdparty code, as it's quite rare that we want to debug issues in those libraries. It could default to `-O1` or even `-O2`.

> I'm mostly wondering about the "timeout waiting for fence" Metal error which seems like a bug, even if the root of the problem is just a slow import due to lacking optimization.

I was not able to reproduce this with any version, only long load time.
First time I encountered this it froze the entire system, not just godot, which happens extremely rarely on macos. So I had to reboot. I didn't wait for 4 minutes but it felt unrecoverable

This doesn't seem to be related to performance, when everything is imported it loads into a black window and stays that way indefinitely, I left it running for 15 minutes:
I can try reproducing this on a different project (it works in an empty project) to see if I can isolate anything specific when I have time.

I have additionally tested it on old M1 MacBook Air and I can reproduce the same, it is spamming `timeout waiting for fence` and going to black. Still not reproducible on M4. So likely hardware specific issue.

reproduced in an empty project, It's msaa

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39c24aa7-8777-4765-9582-2fade641e892

I was looking whether it may be related to #114484, but this one was merged on Feb 5, one day after https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/7dac0bc3be27ee70b1bf6da561e9f14cd92224ef.

Another hunch would be #114075. Could you test with a local revert of it?
I can confirm enabling MSAA on M1 (but not on M4) result in rendering artifacts (in my case screen blinking purple and black, but editor still functional but laggy).

> Another hunch would be https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114075. Could you test with a local revert of it?

Seems to be the case, reverting it fixes the issue.

> Seems to be the case, reverting it fixes the issue.

Yes

CC @stuartcarnie

glslang indirectly to generate SPIR-V anf then SPIRV-Cross to convert SPIR-V to Metal Shader Language
